import { Aside } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

Every app carries an **ABI**: a JSON description of its surface, generated by
`#[app::logic]` at compile time and embedded in the component as the custom
section `calimero:abi`. It is part of the component's bytes, so it is covered by
the bundle's hash and cannot drift from the code it describes.

The node reads it to dispatch and gate calls (`calimero_app_host::Abi::from_json`);
clients read it to learn the methods, arguments and results.

## The format

```json
{
  "abiVersion": 1,
  "world": "calimero:app@0.5.1",
  "state": {
    "fields": { "bookings": "table", "titles": "unorderedMap", "nextId": "counter" },
    "search": { "bookings": [], "nextId": [], "titles": [] },
    "version": 3
  },
  "methods": {
    "book": {
      "kind": "call",
      "params": [["roomId", "string"], ["start", "u64"], ["title", "string"]],
      "returns": "string",
      "confirm": false, "public": false, "allowSystem": false
    },
    "roomCount": {
      "kind": "view",
      "params": [["roomId", "string"]],
      "returns": "u64",
      "confirm": false, "public": true, "allowSystem": false
    },
    "releaseNoShows": {
      "kind": "timer", "params": [], "returns": "option<u64>",
      "every": "1m", "confirm": false, "public": false, "allowSystem": true
    }
  },
  "errors": { "NotFound": {}, "Taken": { "start": "u64" }, "Invalid": { "reason": "string" } },
  "events": { "Booked": { "id": "string", "roomId": "string", "start": "u64" } },
  "types": {
    "Booking": {
      "kind": "record",
      "fields": [["id", "string"], ["roomId", "string"], ["start", "u64"], ["title", "string"], ["checkedIn", "bool"]]
    },
    "Listing": { "kind": "record", "params": ["T"], "fields": [["items", "list<T>"], ["nextCursor", "option<string>"]] },
    "Slot": {
      "kind": "enum", "tag": "state",
      "variants": [{ "name": "free" }, { "name": "held", "fields": [["booking", "Booking"]] }]
    }
  }
}
```

- **`methods`**, by camelCase name. `kind` is `init`, `call`, `view`, `timer`,
  `action` or `compute`. `params` are ordered `[name, type]` pairs. The flags come from the
  [method attributes](/build/sdk-macros/#method-attributes): `confirm`,
  `public` (and `rate`), `allowSystem`, `every` on timers, `allowApps`,
  `allowAction`, `compute` (`fuel`, `memoryMib`, `wallSecs`, `result`) on compute
  methods and `computeResult` on their result methods. A compute method's own
  kind makes a node that does not know compute refuse the bundle rather than
  serve the method as a call.
- **`state`**: each field's kind, the search fields of each table, and the
  `#[app::state(version = N)]`.
- **`errors`** and **`events`**: each code or name with its fields.
- **`types`**: the JSON shape of each app type the methods, errors and events
  name, and of the types those name, by the Rust type's name: every
  `#[derive(Record)]` and every `#[derive(AbiType)]` serde type
  ([SDK macros](/build/sdk-macros/#deriveabitype)). `kind` is `record`
  (`fields` as ordered `[name, type]`, with `{ "optional": true }` third when the
  JSON may leave the field out), `newtype` (`type`), `tuple` (`items`), `unit`, or
  `enum` (`variants`, each `{ name }`, `{ name, type }`, `{ name, items }` or
  `{ name, fields }`, told apart as serde does: by the variant's name as the key,
  by `tag`, by `tag` and `content`, or `untagged`). A generic type lists its
  `params`, which its fields name (`Listing<Slot>` puts `Slot` for `T`). The key
  is absent when no type has a shape, and a type it does not list is unknown.
- **Types**: Rust integer, float and bool names, `string`, `bytes`,
  `option<T>`, `list<T>`, `tuple<..>`, `unit`, else the Rust type's name.
  `u64`, `i64` and `bytes` are strings on the wire. `u64_number`, `i64_number`
  and `byte_list` describe what plain serde writes instead (a field marked
  `#[abi(plain)]`): a JSON number and an array of byte numbers.

Every object's keys are written in sorted order, so the same source always
produces the same bytes.

## What the node enforces

The host reads `abiVersion` (and refuses one it does not support), the method
kinds, and the flags: a view never runs as a write, `confirm` needs a fresh
passkey assertion, `public` admits callers who are not signed in, `allowSystem`,
`allowApps` and `allowAction` admit the node, other apps and the app's own
actions. Free-form keys (`params`, `returns`, `errors`, `events`, `types`) describe the
app to clients; nodes ignore them, so `types` came without an `abiVersion` bump: a
node of an earlier release installs an app that carries it. A field the host enforces is added only with
an `abiVersion` bump.

## Read it

- `GET /apps/{app}/abi` returns an installed app's ABI
  ([Node API](/operate/admin-api/)); `meroctl instance abi` prints it.
- `GET /apps/{app}/openapi.json` returns it as an OpenAPI 3.1 document (below),
  under the same access.
- mero-js and calimero-client-py read it to build typed calls;
  `meroctl app codegen` writes a typed client for an app from it in
  TypeScript, Python, Swift or Kotlin
  ([Typed clients for your app](/build/guides/typed-clients/)).

## As OpenAPI

`calimero_app_abi::openapi` turns an ABI into an OpenAPI 3.1 document. The node
serves the one of the bundle an app runs at `GET /apps/{app}/openapi.json`
(`info.title` the app's name, `info.version` its bundle hash), and
`meroctl app codegen --lang openapi` writes it for a built app.

- **One operation per method a client calls**: `POST /apps/{app}/methods/{name}`,
  `operationId` the method's name, tagged `call` or `view`. Init, timers,
  actions, compute methods, `computeResult` and `allow(action)` methods are left
  out: no client calls them. The node runs this route exactly as `/intents`
  (a call, or a `confirm` view) or `/views` (any other view) with the same
  `method`: the same authentication, gating, step-up and limits.
- **Request**: the body of `/intents` or `/views` without `method`. `args` is the
  parameters by name (`<Method>Args`; an `option<..>` parameter may be left out),
  with `idempotencyKey` (and `confirm` on a `confirm` method) for a call,
  `consistency` and `minIndex` for a view.
- **Answer** (`<Method>Response`): `{ index, result, receipt }`, plus `events` for a
  call; `result` is typed from `returns`.
- **Errors**: `{ error, message, details }`, as the rest of the node API.
  `422` is `APP_ERROR` with `details.code` one of the app's `errors` and
  `details.fields` its fields (`<Code>Error`), or `TRAP`. The ABI lists errors for
  the whole app, so every method documents all of them. A `confirm` method
  documents the `412 CONFIRM_REQUIRED` step-up and its retry with `confirm`;
  a `public` one may be called without a session (`security: [{}, ...]`), and its
  `rate` is in `x-calimero-method`.
- **Events**: `GET /apps/{app}/events` answers `text/event-stream`; each frame's
  `event` is an event's name and `data` its fields (`<Name>Event`). An app with
  actions also gets the node's `ActionFailed { actionId, method, reason }`.
- **Transport**: every request travels inside the node's sealed channel, so a
  client generated from the document needs mero-js, calimero-client-py,
  swift-sdk or kotlin-sdk underneath (the clients `meroctl app codegen` writes
  are built on them).

### Types

The JSON form of every ABI type, as the SDK's macros write and read it (D20):

| ABI type | JSON | JSON Schema |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `bool` | `true` / `false` | `{ "type": "boolean" }` |
| `u8`, `u16`, `u32`, `i8`, `i16`, `i32` | number | `integer` with the type's `minimum`/`maximum` (`format: int32` for `i32`) |
| `usize`, `isize` | number | `integer`, 32-bit range (apps run on wasm32) |
| `u64`, `i64` | **decimal string** (`"18446744073709551615"`) | `string` with a decimal `pattern`; `x-calimero-type` names it |
| `u64_number`, `i64_number` (`#[abi(plain)]`) | number, as plain serde writes it | `integer` with the 64-bit range; past 2^53 JavaScript loses precision |
| `u128`, `i128` | number, only within 64 bits | `integer` with the 64-bit range; past 2^53 JavaScript loses precision, so prefer `u64` or a string |
| `f32`, `f64` | number (no NaN or infinity) | `number`, `format: float` / `double` |
| `char` | a one-character string | `string`, length 1 |
| `string` | string | `string` |
| `bytes` (`Vec<u8>`) | **base64url** without padding | `string`, `contentEncoding: base64url` |
| `byte_list` (`Vec<u8>`, `#[abi(plain)]`) | array of numbers 0..=255 | `array` of `integer` |
| `unit` / `returns: null` | `null` | `{ "type": "null" }` |
| `option<T>` | `T` or `null`; a parameter may be left out | `anyOf: [T, null]`, not `required` |
| `list<T>`, `Vec<T>`, `[T]` | array | `array` of `T` |
| `[T; N]` | array of exactly `N` | `array`, `minItems` = `maxItems` = `N` |
| `BTreeSet<T>`, `HashSet<T>` | array of distinct values | `array`, `uniqueItems` |
| `tuple<A, B>` | array `[a, b]` | `array` with `prefixItems` |
| `BTreeMap<K, V>`, `HashMap<K, V>` | object, keys as strings | `object` with `additionalProperties: V` (integer keys get a `propertyNames` pattern) |
| `Box<T>`, `Rc<T>`, `Arc<T>`, `&T` | as `T` | as `T` |
| any other name (a record, a serde struct or enum, `Page<Item>`) | the type's serde form | a component named after it (`Page_Item`): its shape from `types`, else any JSON |

A `u64`, `i64` or `Vec<u8>` nested inside another type is a compile error
(Ruling 27), so the string forms above hold wherever these types appear. A
`#[derive(AbiType)]` field marked `#[abi(plain)]` is described as plain serde
writes it, at any depth (`Vec<u64>` is `list<u64_number>`): its JSON does not
change, the ABI only says what it is. `list<u8>` still reads as `bytes`;
`byte_list` is the array spelling.
An app type with a shape in `types` is a component with that shape: an object
with its fields, a `oneOf` per enum, a generic type instantiated per use
(`Listing_Slot`). One without (a type with neither derive, or any type in an ABI
built before `types`) is an open schema (`x-calimero-abi-type` keeps the Rust
name) and a typed client types it `unknown` / `Any` / `JSONValue` /
`JsonElement`. The Swift and Kotlin clients make each described type a nested
type: a record a `struct` / `data class`, an enum an `enum` / `sealed interface`
coded in its serde tagging, generic where the Rust type is
([Typed clients](/build/guides/typed-clients/#how-the-types-come-out)).

The Swift and Kotlin clients take the Swift or Kotlin type and write its JSON form
themselves: `u64` is `UInt64` / `ULong`, `i64` `Int64` / `Long`, `bytes` `Data` /
`ByteArray`; `u64_number` / `i64_number` are the same native types written as numbers
(TypeScript `number`, Python `int`), and `byte_list` is `[UInt8]` / `List<UByte>`
(`number[]`, `List[int]`); the other integers keep their width (`u32` is `UInt32` / `UInt`,
`usize` 32 bits, `u128`/`i128` 64 bits), `char` is a `String`, lists, sets and
`[T; N]` are arrays / `List`, maps `[String: V]` / `Map<String, V>`, and
`tuple<A, B>` a `Tuple2<A, B>` that is the JSON array `[a, b]`.

## Check a new version against the last

`meroctl app abi diff <old> <new>` (each a `.wasm`, `.mpk` or ABI JSON) lists
what changed and whether existing callers notice, and exits `1` on a breaking
change; `--json` prints it as JSON. `meroctl app abi show <file>` prints one ABI. Parameters may widen and results narrow:

| Breaking | Compatible |
| --- | --- |
| A method a client, the node or another app calls is removed or renamed (a rename is named) | A method added |
| `kind` changed (a call becomes a view, ...) | An `option<..>` parameter added |
| A parameter removed, added without `option<..>`, or changed to a type that does not hold the old values (`u32` -> `u64` moves from a number to a string) | A parameter widened (`u16` -> `u32`, `T` -> `option<T>`, `char` -> `string`) |
| A result changed to a type outside the old one (`T` -> `option<T>`, `u16` -> `u32`) | A result narrowed (`option<T>` -> `T`), or a method that returned nothing now returns a value |
| `confirm` added; `public`, `allowSystem` or an `allowApps` entry removed; `allow(action)` added | The reverse of each; parameters reordered (JSON passes them by name); `rate`, `every` or compute caps changed |
| An error or event removed, or one of its fields removed or changed outside its old type | An error, event or field added |
| `abiVersion` changed; `world` moved to another minor | `world` moved to another patch |
| A state field removed or its collection kind changed; the state version going down or up by more than one | A state field added; the state version up by one; search fields changed |
| A type's shape in `types` changed in a way its callers notice (below) | A type gaining a shape (it was any JSON) |

The app types the methods, errors and events name, and the types those name, are
compared by name in `types`, in the direction they travel in the old ABI: a type
inside a parameter of a method called from outside is **sent** (it may widen), one
inside a result, error or event is **read** (it may narrow), and a type used both
ways must hold both. Each change is reported as `type <Name>`:

| Change | Sent | Read |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A field added | Breaking unless callers may leave it out (`option<..>` or `optional`) | Compatible |
| A field removed | Breaking | Breaking, unless it was `optional` |
| A field retyped, a variant's payload or a tuple item retyped | Compatible when it widens | Compatible when it narrows |
| A field now `optional` (may be left out) | Compatible | Breaking |
| A field no longer `optional` | Breaking, unless it is an `option<..>` | Compatible |
| A variant added | Compatible | Breaking |
| A variant removed | Breaking | Compatible |
| Fields or variants reordered | Compatible (an `untagged` enum's variants: breaking, serde tries them in order) | Compatible |
| The tagging style, the shape's kind (record, enum, ...), a variant's payload kind, a tuple's length or the number of generic parameters changed | Breaking | Breaking |
| A generic parameter renamed | Compatible | Compatible |
| The type lost its shape | Breaking | Breaking |

Every generated client ignores a key it does not know, so a field added to what
it reads is safe: TypeScript and Python read plain objects, Swift's `Decodable`
skips keys its type does not name, and the Kotlin client decodes with
`Json { ignoreUnknownKeys = true }`. A variant added to what a client reads is
not: a client that decodes the enum exhaustively (a Swift or Kotlin enum, a
`switch` over a TypeScript union) has no case for it. A type the old ABI's callers do not
exchange (only an `allow(action)` method takes it, or nothing names it) is not
compared. Recursive types (`Tree` holding `list<Tree>`) and generic ones
(`Page<T>`, reached as `Page<Item>`) are compared once each.

`meroctl app sign --previous <last release>` (and
`meroctl app pack --previous`) runs the same check before signing: it prints the changes, warns
about breaking ones, and **refuses to sign** when a state field was removed or
changed kind while `#[app::state(version = N)]` stayed the same, since the
upgrade to that release would leave the app's data unreadable
([Upgrades & state](/build/migrations/)).

<Aside type="note">
  Upgrades compare the state section of the two ABIs: see
  [Upgrades & state](/build/migrations/).
</Aside>
